segments.narration: This disc was printed with stamps, not written. Crete, found in nineteen oh eight, fired clay, both sides covered.
Two hundred and forty-one signs spiral inward, and each one was pressed in with its own carved punch.
That makes it a printed document. Reusable type, pressed into clay, thousands of years before a press existed in Europe.
There are forty-five distinct symbols. Heads with feathers, a shield, a fish, a walking figure. No other Cretan text uses them.
With one short text and no bilingual key, decipherment is close to impossible. Some scholars still doubt it is genuine.

verdicts.claim: The disc carries 241 stamped signs arranged in a spiral, impressed with individual punches
verdicts.note: The 241 tokens were made with a set of reusable stamps.

verdicts.claim: Because the signs were made with reusable punches the disc is often described as an early example of movable type
verdicts.note: The stamped production method is widely noted as a precursor of movable type.

verdicts.claim: The disc uses 45 distinct signs that do not match other known Cretan scripts

verdicts.claim: The disc remains undeciphered and its authenticity has occasionally been questioned
